blocks.text: Anthropic 于周一提交的 335 页 S-1 招股书，是硅谷与华尔街互动中一轮持续升温的炒作的最新一环。从某些角度看，这甚至算不上多离谱：SpaceX 在 6 月上市，其 S-1 文件里提到了恐龙和“殖民火星”。但这份文件措辞宏大、篇幅惊人——光风险因素就写了 94 页——AI 行业的豪言壮语与硬核的融资推介撞在一起，有时让人难以招架。那些天花乱坠的承诺，对Anthropic 这家公司的存续而言不可或缺。但这并不妨碍读这份 S-1 时感到荒诞。

blocks.text: 在信中，Anthropic 的创始人劝潜在股东“不要把你的购买纯粹看作一笔交易。我们希望你能把它视为参与更宏大事业的机会”。信中说，迈向先进 AI 的进程“是人类历史上最重要的时刻之一”，“我们的目标是帮助人类在这场技术演进中安全航行，开辟新的发现前沿，开启一个奇迹时代”。但 S-1 同时警告，一旦出事，后果可能是灾难性的——甚至构成对人类的“生存性”风险。文件不厌其详地列出了诸多危险，包括模型“以用户和开发者都未曾预料的方式行事”，进而引发“灾难性”事件，其损失之大，整个保险业都无力承保。

blocks.text: Anthropic’s 335-page S-1 prospectus, filed Monday, is part of a steady hype escalation in Silicon Valley’s interactions with Wall Street. In some ways, it’s not even that bizarre; SpaceX IPO’d in June after filing an S-1 that referenced dinosaurs and “colonizing Mars.” But its sweeping language and sheer volume — including 94 pages of risk factors — is a sometimes overwhelming collision of AI industry rhetoric and a hard financial pitch. Out-of-this-world promises are integral to Anthropic’s survival as a company. That doesn’t make reading the S-1 any less surreal.

blocks.text: In the letter, Anthropic’s founders urge prospective stock owners “not to think of your purchase in purely transactional terms. We hope you will see it instead as an opportunity to be part of something greater.” The march toward advanced AI “is one of the seminal moments in human history,” the letter says. “Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles.” But the S-1 warns that if things go wrong, the consequences could be disastrous — even an “existential” risk to humanity. Many dangers are laid out in exhaustive detail, including risks that models “behave in ways that no user or developer intended,” leading to “catastrophic” incidents that the entire insurance industry couldn’t afford to underwrite.

blocks.text: The heart of Anthropic’s pitch — or anti-sell — is that despite the risks, it is absolutely committed to developing safe and secure AI technology. After all, it will go public as a public benefit corporation, a type of business entity that, unlike C-corporations that are required to maximize shareholder value, must prioritize a social mission alongside shareholder interests.

blocks.text: “Powerful AI” — Anthropic’s term for hypothetical future AI that surpasses collective human intelligence — is presented in the company’s S-1 as inevitable. If this technology is coming no matter what, then Anthropic, a public benefit corporation, should lead the charge. But Anthropic will need a lot of money, possibly an unlimited amount, to do this. And more practically, as Liz Lopatto has written, powerful AI (in the form of dramatic recursive self-improvement) might be about the only way Anthropic can stay ahead of the competition and survive.

blocks.text: For all the information the company made available in its S-1, there are some gaps. Crucial information that could be used to assess profitability — third quarter results, for instance — is missing. Anthropic saw explosive revenue growth in the second quarter, but the second quarter was also the height of tokenmaxxing, which could have led to a surge in sales. Some corporate executives have warned that AI costs are surging out of control. While Anthropic’s operating losses narrowed in the second quarter, the S-1 also revealed hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations to secure the computing power it says it needs to keep growing. It also said it will start building its own data center infrastructure, a costly move that would eat into profit.
